title: On‑Prem Air‑Gap Test Plan — Private Observability Minimum Pack
content:
Doc purpose
Validate that the “Private observability minimum pack” can be installed and operated in a fully air‑gapped on‑prem lab with no external network egress, using only pre-staged artifacts (charts/images/bundles), and that the resulting deployment meets Redwood’s “supported signals” bar (dashboards load, rules load, logs/metrics flow, and validation checks pass).

Owner / DRI
- DRI: Fatima Noor (On‑prem/air‑gapped packaging SME)
- Implementation partners: Bruno Silva (installer), Sahana Iyer (CI/validation), Sergio Costa (dashboards/alerts)
- Reviewers for go/no‑go: Sean Gallagher (SRE paging policy), Naomi Feldman (security defaults), Dev Patel (support readiness)

Scope
In scope for this test plan
- Air‑gapped install path for:
  - Private installer
  - Observability pack bundle (dashboards + rules + logging defaults)
  - Supported third‑party components (Prometheus + Grafana + log forwarder) running in-cluster or as part of the lab setup
- Day‑1 validation: “supported signals” checks, dashboards render, alerts parse and are evaluated, log pipeline is healthy
- Upgrade/rollback sanity (single step): pack version bump and rollback in air‑gapped mode

Out of scope
- Customer-specific SIEM connectors beyond the baseline supported targets
- Long-retention analytics/backfills
- HA sizing/perf benchmarking beyond basic load sanity

Assumptions / constraints (air‑gap)
- No internet access from cluster nodes (no Docker Hub, no public Helm repos, no OS package mirrors).
- Only allowed ingress: operator laptop to a “staging host” (jumpbox) on the same isolated network.
- Any registries/repos must be hosted inside the air‑gapped network (e.g., local OCI registry, local chart repo, file-based bundles).
- TLS: self‑signed or lab CA is acceptable, but all components must run with TLS enabled where supported by defaults.

Test environments
Lab A (minimal footprint) — primary
- K8s: 3 nodes
- Storage: local PV or NFS inside lab
- Local registry: Harbor or registry:2 inside lab
- Grafana + Prometheus deployed via bundled charts
- Log collector: Vector or Fluent Bit (per current pack default)

Lab B (upgrade/rollback rehearsal)
- Same as Lab A but used to validate upgrade/rollback procedure without contaminating the primary baseline

Artifacts required (must be staged before unplugging)

1) Redwood Private artifacts
- redwood-private-installer binary (or container image, depending on packaging)
- Private Helm charts bundle (tgz) OR installer embedded charts
- Version manifest for Private installer and chart versions
- Any CRDs required for Private components

2) Observability pack artifacts
- observability-pack bundle (offline):
  - Grafana dashboards JSON (provisioning layout: folders + datasources + dashboards)
  - PrometheusRule YAML bundles + any recording rules
  - Log pipeline default configs (Vector/Fluent Bit) + redaction/sampling defaults
  - Pack version manifest (e.g., pack.yaml)
- SHA256 checksums for all bundle files

3) Container images (mirrored)
- Redwood Private images (gateway, runtime, control plane, installer/upgrade controller)
- Grafana image(s)
- Prometheus image(s) (Prometheus + kube-state-metrics + node-exporter if used)
- Log agent image(s) (Vector and/or Fluent Bit depending on chosen default)
- Any sidecars used by the pack (dashboards provisioning init, rule reloader, etc.)
- Optional: a “mock” SIEM endpoint image if we test forwarding to HTTP inside lab

4) Offline dependencies
- Helm binary (if not embedded)
- kubectl
- promtool (optional but recommended for debugging in lab)
- A “golden config” values.yaml for this test plan

Pre‑flight checklist (before air‑gap)
- [ ] Confirm final artifact list + checksums are stored on operator laptop and on staging host
- [ ] Confirm local registry is installed and reachable from all cluster nodes
- [ ] Confirm all required images are pushed to local registry and pull works from cluster (test with a dummy pod)
- [ ] Confirm charts can be installed from file:// paths (no remote refs)
- [ ] Confirm no chart values reference external URLs (Grafana plugins, dashboards, prom rules)
- [ ] Confirm TLS certs are available (lab CA) and secrets can be created offline

Test matrix

Legend
- P0 = must pass for “supported” air‑gapped Private install
- P1 = should pass; failure requires escalation/bug filed
- P2 = nice-to-have; track as follow-up

Matrix
ID | Priority | Area | Test | Expected result
---|----------|------|------|----------------
A1 | P0 | Packaging | Offline bundle integrity | Bundle checksums match; manifest present; unpack succeeds
A2 | P0 | Registry | Local registry image availability | All images pull from local registry; no external pulls observed
A3 | P0 | Install | Private base install (air‑gapped) | Private components running Ready; no CrashLoopBackOff
A4 | P0 | Install | Observability pack install (air‑gapped) | Dashboards/rules/configs applied; installer reports success
A5 | P0 | Metrics | Prometheus scrape health | Targets UP for gateway/runtime/control plane/installer health
A6 | P0 | Dashboards | Grafana provisioning | Datasource configured; dashboards appear in expected folders; no “missing datasource” errors
A7 | P0 | Alerts | Rule loading & evaluation | PrometheusRule objects created; Prometheus loads rules; no parse errors
A8 | P0 | Logs | Structured logs flowing | Gateway/runtime/control plane logs ingested with required fields; redaction applied
A9 | P0 | Validation | Post-install validation command | Installer validation passes; exports report artifact
A10| P0 | Security | Auth/TLS defaults | Grafana not anonymously writable; TLS enabled per defaults; no secrets in ConfigMaps
A11| P1 | Alerts | “Missing signals” alert group | Fires when we intentionally break a scrape/log pipeline; resolves after fix
A12| P1 | Logs | Forwarding target inside air‑gap | Logs forward to lab sink (e.g., HTTP endpoint or object storage) without drops
A13| P1 | Perf sanity | Load test smoke | Under small synthetic load, dashboards show expected RPS/latency; no sustained queue runaway
A14| P1 | Upgrade | Pack upgrade (N -> N+1) | Upgrade completes; dashboards/rules updated; no data loss beyond expected
A15| P1 | Rollback | Pack rollback (N+1 -> N) | Rollback completes; rules still load; Grafana stable
A16| P2 | Ops | Day‑2 rotation | Operator can rotate Grafana admin creds + verify access logs (if enabled) without breaking provisioning

Step-by-step lab procedure

Phase 0 — Prepare air‑gapped lab network
1) Bring up staging host (jumpbox) inside isolated network.
2) Bring up local registry inside isolated network.
   - Record: REGISTRY_HOST, REGISTRY_PORT, registry CA (if TLS)
3) Bring up Kubernetes cluster nodes; verify nodes can reach local registry.
4) Confirm no egress.
   - Simple check: from a pod, attempt to resolve/ping a public endpoint; it should fail.

Phase 1 — Stage artifacts and mirror images
1) Copy artifacts to staging host:
   - private-installer
   - private charts bundle
   - observability-pack bundle
   - checksums
   - tools (kubectl/helm/promtool)
2) Load/push images into the local registry.
   - Use the provided image list file (images.txt) and mirror script.
   - Verify:
     - “docker pull REGISTRY/.../grafana:<tag>” works from node runtime
     - “kubectl run” test pod can pull an image from REGISTRY
3) Update the “golden values.yaml” to point to local registry.
   - Ensure all image.repository fields are REGISTRY_HOST/namespace/name

Phase 2 — Install Prometheus + Grafana (offline)
Note: If the Private installer deploys these for the min pack, this phase becomes “verify they are deployed”. If customer-managed is required, install from bundled charts.
1) Install Prometheus stack from local chart tgz.
2) Install Grafana from local chart tgz.
3) Configure Grafana datasource to point to the in-cluster Prometheus.
4) Verify:
   - Prometheus UI reachable inside lab
   - Grafana UI reachable inside lab
   - Grafana admin password set via secret (not default)

Phase 3 — Install Redwood Private (air‑gapped)
1) Run private installer with air‑gapped flags.
   - Example (illustrative; adjust to actual CLI):
     - redwood-private install --offline-bundle /artifacts/private-bundle.tgz --registry REGISTRY_HOST --values /artifacts/lab-values.yaml
2) Wait for all namespaces and deployments to become Ready.
3) Verify core:
   - Gateway responding to /healthz
   - Runtime service endpoints up
   - Control plane health endpoints up

Phase 4 — Install observability minimum pack (air‑gapped)
1) Run installer step or helm apply for the observability pack:
   - Example: redwood-private observability install --pack-bundle /artifacts/observability-pack.tgz
2) Confirm provisioning objects are created:
   - ConfigMaps/Secrets for Grafana provisioning
   - PrometheusRule resources
   - Log agent DaemonSet / Deployment
3) Verify:
   - Grafana shows “Private / Gateway Overview”, “Runtime Performance”, “GPU Saturation”, “Control Plane Health”, “Private Install Health” (exact names per current pack)
   - Prometheus shows rule groups loaded; no errors in /status

Phase 5 — Validate signals
Metrics validation (P0)
- Confirm scrape targets UP for:
  - gateway
  - runtime
  - control plane
  - installer/upgrade controller (installer health)
- Run a minimal set of queries in Prometheus (examples; exact metric names may differ by final contract):
  - rate(http_requests_total[5m]) by (job)
  - histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
  - up{job=~".*redwood.*"}
- Pass criteria: targets stable UP; query returns data within 5 minutes of install

Dashboard validation (P0)
- Open each dashboard and confirm:
  - Variables populate (model/route/tenant where applicable)
  - Panels render without “N/A due to missing series” for baseline panels (some workload-dependent panels may be empty until load)
  - No Grafana provisioning errors in Grafana logs

Alerting validation (P0/P1)
- Confirm Prometheus loaded all rules:
  - No prom rule parse errors
  - Rule evaluation running
- Induce a controlled failure (P1):
  - Temporarily block scraping of one target (NetworkPolicy or scale to 0)
  - Confirm “missing signals” alert fires within expected time window
  - Restore target; confirm alert resolves

Logs validation (P0)
- Confirm log agent running on all nodes.
- Confirm log entries for gateway/runtime/control plane are present with structured fields:
  - request_id
  - tenant (if applicable)
  - model
  - route
  - error_code
  - severity/level
- Confirm redaction/safety:
  - No raw Authorization headers
  - No full prompts/completions unless explicitly configured (default should be safe)

Validation command (P0)
- Run post-install validation command (if available):
  - Example: redwood-private observability validate --output /tmp/validation-report.json
- Confirm it checks:
  - Grafana API reachability
  - Prometheus rule load status
  - Presence of required metrics
  - Log pipeline health
- Save report artifact for the results section.

Phase 6 — Upgrade/rollback rehearsal (P1)
Upgrade
1) Stage new pack bundle version (N+1) on staging host.
2) Run upgrade step.
3) Verify dashboards/rules updated; Prometheus still loads rules.
Rollback
1) Roll back to pack version N.
2) Verify stability; no lingering config references to N+1 assets.

Failure triage notes (quick)
- If PrometheusRule fails to load: check Prometheus logs for parse errors; run promtool check rules on the rule files inside the pack bundle.
- If Grafana dashboards missing: check provisioning paths/ConfigMap mounts; verify Grafana has permissions to read mounted files.
- If log drops: check agent buffer/backpressure metrics; ensure forwarding target reachable; reduce sampling only as a last resort.
- If installer cannot find bundles: verify absolute paths and that the installer supports “local artifact path” mode in air‑gap.

Pass/fail criteria (release gate)
P0 must pass:
- A1–A10
If any P0 fails:
- Stop and file a blocking bug (link Linear), include logs + validation report.

P1 expectations:
- A11–A15 should pass; if not, must have documented workaround and explicit sign-off from DRI + SRE lead for GA.

Open questions / TODOs
- Confirm the “supported” default log forwarding target for on‑prem air‑gap (HTTP sink vs object storage vs customer SIEM). For this plan we can validate to an in-lab HTTP endpoint + optional S3-compatible object store if available.
- Confirm whether Grafana plugins are required by any dashboard panels; if yes, plugins must be vendored or avoided (no external download).
- Finalize exact metric names/labels required for the dashboards (route/model/tenant) and update the queries in the validation section once the contract is locked.
